children: London shares inched higher on Wednesday as oil retreated, while traders awaited the key U.S. Federal Reserve decision on interest rate hikes due later this day.
The blue-chip FTSE 100 index
CURRENCYCOM:UK100
rose 0.34% to 10,692.21 points by 0926 GMT, while the midcap FTSE 250
climbed 0.46%.
Oil prices retreated after a two-day rally after reports of additional Saudi crude cargoes via Oman eased Middle East supply concerns.
Homebuilders (.FTNMX402020) rallied 4.4%, led by Barratt Redrow
, which gained 8.8%, after reporting stronger reservation rates, a robust order book and profit above forecasts.
On the data front, British inflation accelerated to a five-month high of 3.1% in August, though price growth, excluding surging energy costs, remained stable, official figures showed.

Investors are more focused on the Federal Reserve's decision on interest rate hikes later in the day, with traders pricing in a 92% chance of a 25-basis-point hike, according to the CME's FedWatch tool.

Meanwhile, the Bank of England is slated to announce its rate decision tomorrow. Traders expect the BoE to hold interest rates steady at this meeting but still see at least a 43.9-basis-point rise priced in by year-end, according to LSEG-compiled data.

"Near term, AI and oil jitters may help FTSE100, and while domestic macro is tricky, valuations offer cushion,​‌", Barclays analysts said in a note as the index is up 7.6% this year, in line with the STOXX, even after a recent pull-back as bond yields and oil prices surged.
Rate-sensitive heavyweight banks (.FTNMX301010) gained 1.6% with HSBC
rising 1.3% and Standard Chartered
adding 2.2%.
Unilever
shed 1.4% after UK competition regulators launched a competition probe into its proposed merger with McCormick
Among mid-caps, greeting card retailer Moonpig
fell 5.8% despite maintaining its annual outlook, with analysts pointing to consumer spending concerns and profit-taking.
